items.author: John Peterson
items.text:
I hated on @bryanbrosgolf and @wesleybryangolf for years about YouTube golf…to the point where I started to genuinely believe what they were doing was elementary and it would never catch on. 

Then Wesley called me and asked me to be a wild card for Purcell farms on the @YourGolfTourYGT. I had to ask him what it was….when I found out it was YouTube golf I initially laughed and rejected it but figured if I’d ever form a concrete opinion on it I needed to see for myself. 

I went and was shocked by it all. Not just the quality of golf but the venue, the family feel it has and the millions of people that tune into wholesome entertainment they aren’t afraid to leave on for their kids. That’s the biggest deal-YouTube golf is for everyone. 

No longer a hater, and thrilled for y’all to see what we cooked up at the Wynn in Vegas. 🔥 

Long live YouTube golf 🤙

items.author: Preethi Kasireddy
items.text:
"My husband's semen analysis came back normal"

Okay but did anyone check his homocysteine?

A semen analysis counts his sperm. It can't see whether their DNA is damaged. In a study with 5,032 men, those with the highest homocysteine had 2x the odds of damaged sperm DNA, 20% vs 11%.

If you're trying to conceive, ask for a sperm DNA fragmentation test. Under 15% is ideal, and 15 to 25% is fair. And get his homocysteine checked. It's a cheap blood test, and high levels often mean he's low on folate, B12, or B6.
